title: Soft schema tolerance oracle and experiment harness
creator: Asha Patel
description: When enforcing strict JSON mode and constrained decoding for structured outputs, streaming partials, model variance, and interleaved tool calls can cause hard failures that break downstream consumers. This ticket builds an experiment harness and oracle for a 'soft tolerance' policy: the runtime will attempt constrained decoding first, emit structured events for valid partials, and fall back to a deterministic remediation path (graceful-lax parser, re-request with modified sampling seed, or model-variant fallback) while logging rich telemetry and attaching a grade to the output that downstream clients can use to decide whether to accept, retry, or request reconciliation.
motivation: Reduce customer-facing errors from strict schema enforcement in streaming scenarios while preserving strong guarantees for most well-formed responses. Provide measurable trade-offs (latency/cost vs. schema adherence) and a reproducible testbed for evaluating fallback strategies across model families and prompt templates.
acceptance_criteria: A test harness exists that can simulate streaming partial outputs, token corruption, toolcall interleaving, and model-variant responses
The harness implements three configurable soft-tolerance strategies: emit-partial-events, graceful-lax-parse, and model-variant-fallback
Instrumented telemetry surfaces a 'schema_adherence_score' for each response and a breakdown (parse_failures, repairs_attempted, final_strategy)

Downstream contract: when score >= 0.9 runtime marks response as 'verified'; when 0.6<=score<0.9 marks 'degraded' with remediation_hint; below 0.6 marks 'retry_recommended' and triggers a retry policy in the harness
End-to-end experimental runs show reduced hard-errors by >=60% for simulated partial-stream scenarios with max added latency under 120ms for graceful-lax-parse path
PR with tests and CI integration merged and a public experiment dashboard linked in ticket
test_plan: Unit tests for oracle evaluator (deterministic scoring for constrained-decoding outcomes)
Simulated streaming runs: 10k scenarios across model sizes (small/medium/large) and three prompt families, record per-scenario strategy and outcome
Chaos tests: inject token-level corruption and toolcall interleaving and ensure fallback paths do not crash the serving process
Compatibility check: validate that clients receiving 'degraded' outputs can handle remediation_hint and that SDK surfaces the score
Performance benchmarks: measure latency and token cost for each strategy vs strict-enforce baseline
steps_to_reproduce: Checkout experiment harness branch (link in artifacts) and run `./harness/run_stream_sim --scenarios 1000 --strategy emit-partial-events`
Observe harness logging: partial-event batches, schema_adherence_score, and final_strategy per-request
Trigger token corruption mode `--corrupt 0.02` and repeat; compare failure rates against strict-enforce baseline
Open the dashboard (link in artifacts) to review aggregate metrics and trace samples for failures
expected_behavior: Constrained decoder attempts to produce JSON strictly; if it fails within the streaming window the soft-tolerance layer evaluates best remediation
Emit-partial-events should surface well-formed subsections to consumers without blocking the stream
Graceful-lax-parse attempts a minimal repair using deterministic heuristics and yields a score and repair diff
Model-variant-fallback re-invokes a compatible model variant with identical seed and logs delta in tokens/cost
No strategy should cause serving process crashes or exceed resource budgets defined in performance guidelines
implementation_notes: Start by reusing the constrained-decoder interface used by jsonmode-enforcer but add a non-blocking observer that can calculate partial scores
Keep repair heuristics deterministic and documented; avoid ML-based repair in this phase to keep reproducibility high
Expose score and strategy in trace/span attributes and wire into console rollup so PMs can create alerts on score regressions
Add SDK flag `accept_degraded_outputs` and ensure default remains false until feature gate opens for a beta cohort
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: downstream apps accept degraded outputs silently - Mitigation: SDK opt-in and dashboard showing which customers enabled degraded acceptance
Risk: added latency from retries - Mitigation: configure aggressive timeouts and prioritize low-latency repair strategies first
Risk: telemetry volume increase - Mitigation: sample 1% of low-severity flows and upsample failures for triage
